notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix. §1985:VI.6.26.2 prints three formats: Format 1, SUBTRACT one or more identifier-1 or literal-1 FROM one or more identifier-2 [ROUNDED]; Format 2, the same subtrahends FROM one identifier-2 or literal-2 GIVING one or more identifier-3 [ROUNDED]; Format 3, SUBTRACT CORRESPONDING or CORR identifier-1 FROM identifier-2 [ROUNDED]; each ends with the ON SIZE ERROR phrase, the NOT ON SIZE ERROR phrase and END-SUBTRACT, in that order and each optional. subtractStatement parses the superset and BindSubtract narrows it at every edition (COBOL1689): a missing FROM, a second FROM operand or a ROUNDED on it with GIVING (GivingSendingOperand), a literal FROM operand without GIVING (Format1Receivers); BindSubtractCorresponding binds Format 3, whose grammar alternative admits neither GIVING nor a second receiver. ROUNDED MODE IS is refused at 85 by VisitRoundedPhrase (COBOL0803). All probed at --std 85. What is NOT implemented is the printed sequence of the two phrases: the conditionalPhrases loop and Associates / MayAssociate ask only that a phrase is one the statement's formats print and is not yet written, with no edition arm, so the NOT phrase written before its positive twin compiles and runs at 85; either order is the 2002 change §2002:F.2 (item 33), which the row's change record names. Same mechanism as the ADD, MULTIPLY, STRING and UNSTRING rows of this slice. The witness runs the three formats with the phrases in the printed order.

next.reason: 1985: "[ ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-1 ] [ NOT ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-2 ] ... identifier-2 [ ROUNDED ]"; 2023: "size-error group in choice indicators (zero or more, any order); { identifier-2 [ rounded-phrase ] }". 2023 lets NOT ON SIZE ERROR precede ON SIZE ERROR, which the fixed 1985 order refuses. It also replaces plain ROUNDED with rounded-phrase (14.7.4), which allows added options.
